overall_why: I would use Godot again for a similar game. A text project, a headless SceneTree script, and one windowed capture were enough to build the sim, the HUD, and a proof that checks determinism, a fresh-process save, and an offline hour, with no addons. The score stays at 7 because the long part of the work was engine defaults that report success while wrong: the glTF importer does not apply COLOR_0 as albedo, a one-sided ground plane draws nothing from above, and a script that fails to parse can still quit 0.

docs: Godot 4.7 names the filmic mapper `Environment.TONE_MAPPER_FILMIC`. `TONE_MAP_FILMIC` does not exist. One parse error.
Daylight shots were white. glTF base factors are white and the PNGs are grey masks; the paint is COLOR_0, and the importer leaves `vertex_color_use_as_albedo` off.
loop: GDScript will not infer a type from an untyped RefCounted return, so the proof needed explicit types on every sim local. ... Cost: a handful of headless reruns.
Iterations to a passing proof: the rule proof was already green before the picture was. This visual pass took three framing captures and four full `sh proof/run_proof.sh` runs.
Pixel looks: arrival against `reference/arrival.png` five times, then shop, backpack, market, grown, rain, night, and thunder.
debugging: A script that failed to parse still quit 0 while `fails` stayed empty, and an early "LOGIC PASS" was false until the dump files existed.
`plant_at` was inferred as null, and every subscript of it failed to parse. Declaring the return as Variant fixed it. One rebuild.
The meadow is a one-sided 600 m plane. From above it drew nothing, so the "ground" was the sky colour (exact background RGB).
assets: Vertex colours were in the glTF and the importer left `vertex_color_use_as_albedo` off, so day shots were pale grey. The meadow plane was also culled from above until cull was disabled.
`harvest.wav` imported as "no loader" until a second `godot --import`. A few minutes.
Vertex green is about (32, 73, 8), so the meadow albedo is lifted in place. The texture and the vertices are still the kit. Two recaptures.

Rain parented to the camera, and `emitting = false` left streaks alive for their lifetime, so a clear night still showed rain. Hide the particle node, and restart it when a spell begins.
This visual pass took three framing captures and four full `sh proof/run_proof.sh` runs.

top_frictions: The glTF importer leaves COLOR_0 unused unless vertex_color_use_as_albedo is set, so painted models render as pale grey with no error.
A SceneTree proof can print LOGIC PASS and exit 0 when a preloaded script failed to parse and never ran.
Imported one-sided planes are invisible from above, and GPUParticles keep drawing after emitting is set false for their whole lifetime.
keep: Headless `-s` scripts, an overridable clock, a fresh process, and JSON save made determinism, catch-up, and state asserts possible without looking at pixels.
Text scenes and GDScript were enough for the whole 3D game and a real Control HUD, with no editor session and no addons.
When a script does load, parse errors name the file and the bad type on the next run.
